All 24 graded assertions passed across candidate_skill, released_skill, and no_skill for both evals, so the measured pass rate does not discriminate skill value: every configuration is 1.0 with zero variance.

Eval 1 exposes a conservative-status difference that the assertions miss. candidate_skill sets Validation to independently-validated, but its own grading claim marks that level unverified because the prompt supplies a real CLI exercise without an independent rerun or reviewer. released_skill uses contributor-validated and explicitly preserves independent validation as unknown.

Eval 1 no_skill passes despite not using the schema 2 case contract. It emits custom fields such as case_status, verification_status, and a nested target object instead of the canonical Case schema, Status, Validation, Maintainer acceptance, Knowledge disposition, and Knowledge target fields.

Eval 1 no_skill also uses supports as the case-to-pattern evidence relationship. supports is a skill relationship, while case evidence must use origin, application, evaluation, transfer, contradiction, or rejection. candidate_skill and released_skill both use the valid active application relationship.

The Eval 1 reciprocal-link assertion is too permissive in practice: no_skill says to add a case-side supports link and explicitly says not to change the compiled pattern body, yet the grader still passes it as a reciprocal projection or provenance update. It does not add the required active evidence backlink on foundry/knowledge/patterns/drive-the-shipped-surface.md.

Eval 2 no_skill passes after spelling the disposition as no_change and the target as compiled_knowledge:none. Those are not validator-accepted schema values; the required exact pair is no-change with literal target none. Semantic normalization in grading hides the typed-value error.

Eval 2 candidate_skill selects the correct no-change and none pair and conservative observed, unvalidated, pending, pending, local axes, but omits Case schema: 2 and the canonical Visibility, Repository, Role, and Source fields. Eval 2 no_skill omits canonical Validation and Delivery entirely. The four assertions do not test full schema completeness.

The released_skill outputs are the most conservative about missing retrieval authority: Eval 1 leaves Repository and Source unknown and blocks canonical materialization until public handles exist; Eval 2 chooses an approved-private destination and refuses to fabricate a path. The assertions do not distinguish this from candidate_skill placeholders or no_skill invented case paths.

The grading files themselves reveal the coverage gap: candidate_skill Eval 1 records one verified:false claim for independently-validated status while still awarding 4 of 4 assertions, and released_skill graders separately note that validation level, complete status axes, retrieval handles, confidentiality, and explicit file impact are underchecked.

Timing and resource comparisons are unavailable. Every run records time_seconds 0.0, tokens 0, and tool_calls 0, so the reported +0.0 and +0 deltas are placeholders rather than evidence of equal efficiency.

Benchmark metadata says runs_per_configuration is 3, but benchmark.json contains only one run per eval and configuration, all labeled run_number 1. The resulting zero standard deviations reflect one observed run per cell, not demonstrated repeatability.
